question.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $y,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the constant multiple rule and the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy\operatorname{tan}⁡({y}^{2})) \\  & =x\frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{tan}⁡({y}^{2})) \\  & =x(\frac{∂}{∂y}(y)\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({y}^{2})+y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{tan}⁡({y}^{2}))) \\  & =x((1)\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({y}^{2})+y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{tan}⁡({y}^{2}))) \\  & =x\operatorname{tan}⁡({y}^{2})+xy\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{tan}⁡({y}^{2}))\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the chain rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}x\operatorname{tan}⁡({y}^{2})+xy\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{tan}⁡({y}^{2})) & =x\operatorname{tan}⁡({y}^{2})+xy\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{tan}⁡({y}^{2})) \\  & =x\operatorname{tan}⁡({y}^{2})+xy\cdot {sec}^{2}⁡({y}^{2})\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}) \\  & =x\operatorname{tan}⁡({y}^{2})+xy{sec}^{2}⁡({y}^{2})\cdot (2y) \\  & =x\operatorname{tan}⁡({y}^{2})+2x{y}^{2}{sec}^{2}⁡({y}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$
